question: In Rutherford’s $\alpha$-particle scattering experiment, most of the $\alpha$-particles passed through the gold foil without any appreciable deflection, while a very small number were deflected through large angles. Explain what conclusions about the structure of the atom follow from these observations.

options.A: Most $\alpha$-particles passed undeflected, showing that positive charge is uniformly spread throughout the atom. Large deflections show that electrons are concentrated at the centre.
options.B: All parts of the atom are filled with positive charge, so the atom is a solid sphere. The large deflections occur because $\alpha$-particles collide with electrons.
options.C: Most $\alpha$-particles passed through without deflection, showing that most of the atom is empty space. The few large-angle deflections show that the positive charge and most of the mass are concentrated in a tiny, massive, positively charged central nucleus.
options.D: Most $\alpha$-particles passed undeflected because the nucleus occupies most of the atom. Large deflections show that negative charge is concentrated at the centre.
